h: Ha’azinu Unites the Written and Oral Torah in Every Soul

p: "Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak,
וְתִשְׁמַע הָאָרֶץ אִמְרֵי פִי (דְּבָרִים לב, א)
and let the earth hear the sayings of my mouth" (Devarim 32:1).
that it does not say "and hear, O earth."
Also, of the heavens it writes "and I will speak,"
and of the earth "the sayings of my mouth,"
and it does not say "my words."
'and to the earth, to judge His people'
And this is what it says of this song,
it refers to the whole Torah;
וְעַתָּה כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת
"And now write for yourselves this song,"
whose plain sense refers to the song of Ha'azinu,
from it the positive commandment is learned
And this is because in this song
all the souls of Yisrael are included,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשֵׁם הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as is written in the name of the Ramban, of blessed memory;
and the six hundred thousand souls of Yisrael
are the six hundred thousand letters of the Torah.
And of this it says "and I will speak":
And this is why it uses the term "speech,"
as it is written, 'and He spoke,' etc.,
for one must incline the ear to words of Torah,
and the Written Torah would have sufficed,
only the five books of the Torah," etc.
that it is the Oral Torah
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
And as it will be in the future,
וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ
"And they will no longer teach, each man his fellow."
And this is "and let the earth hear":
that the earth will hear of itself,
in which Adam HaRishon was clothed
in which there is an evil inclination,
And this is what is said, "the sayings of my mouth":
we call her the Oral Torah.

p: It says "the sayings of my mouth,"
"My teaching shall drop like the rain":
this refers to the Written Torah,
"For I have given you good teaching";
which is evidently coming down from heaven.
"My saying shall flow like the dew":
this refers to the Oral Torah,
whose descent from heaven is not evident;
only from seeing that the ground is moist
do we understand that dew came down from above.
to be what they innovate from their own hearts,
the words of the living God,
דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְּפִיךָ (יְשַׁעְיָה נט, כא)
"My words that I have placed in your mouth" (Yeshayahu 59:21),
which Hashem Yisbarach shines into the heart of the Sages.
And therefore it is called amirah,
"And you will say in your heart";
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רלד, ב)
כִּי שֵׁם ה׳ אֶקְרָא וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם, ג)
"For I will proclaim the Name of Hashem," etc. (Devarim 32:3):
this refers to the Written Torah,
is the Name of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צח, ב)
and this is why there is learned from this pasuk
the blessing over the Torah before it
"That is 'they did not listen to My voice,'
that is 'they did not walk in it,'" etc.,
"that they do not bless over the Torah first."
For the essence of the Oral Torah
is to sense taste in the Written Torah;
And when they do not bless,
it means they learned without desire and taste;
and they do not merit children who are Torah scholars.

p: And this parshah is read before Sukkos,
עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ג)
according to what is said (Shir HaShirim 2:3):
"In His shade I delighted and sat,
and His fruit was sweet to my palate."
Yisrael were likened to an apple tree,
"and His fruit was sweet to my palate";
for HaKadosh Baruch Hu is likened to an apple tree,
for Hashem Yisbarach is the trunk of the apple tree,
are the fruit of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב רכג, ב)
(as written in the holy Zohar II 223b):
It is the souls of the righteous,
of the works of HaKadosh Baruch Hu."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א פה, ב)
And as written (in the holy Zohar I 85b);
and of this it is said,
"and His fruit was sweet to my palate";
the apples themselves are Knesses Yisrael;
And it is written, "In His shade I delighted and sat":
the sukkos, the Clouds of Glory.
And in the holy Zohar (II there):
sits in the shade of God,
"the spreading of the shelter of peace over us
and over all His people Yisrael":
And this parshah is the last parshah
for Parshas Berachah is read on Yom Tov
there are counted in the holy Zohar
for from there begins the Oral Torah.
And it is read on Yom Tov,
And therefore this parshah is read,
and the Oral Torah, as stated,
"In His shade I delighted and sat":
the shade of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
"and His fruit was sweet to my palate":
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah:
בְּשַׁבָּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל (שַׁבָּת פו, ב)
that the Torah was given to Yisrael on Shabbos (Shabbos 86b);
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 47b);
